title: _weighted_percentile: read weights from sorted_weights (NaN weights zeroed), not raw sample_weight
answers: _weighted_percentile returns nan with average=True when the data contains NaNs
weighted median / percentile 100 gives nan even though NaNs should be ignored
why does _weighted_percentile use sorted_weights instead of sample_weight
body:
Symptom: `_weighted_percentile(..., average=True)` on an array with NaNs returns nan at percentile_rank=100. NaNs are supposed to be ignored.
Root cause: sklearn/utils/stats.py:_weighted_percentile ignores NaNs by setting their weight to 0 on the sorted copy `sorted_weights`. The average=True branch that looks for a zero-weight 'plus one' neighbour indexed the original `sample_weight`, where the NaN still has its nonzero weight. NaNs sort last, so only the top percentile could land on one.
Fix pattern: after sorting and masking NaNs, take every weight lookup from `sorted_weights[sorted_idx, col_indices]`. Never index back into the unsorted `sample_weight` with sorted indices.
Constraints: this applies to any new branch added to _weighted_percentile, whether average or not. NaN bugs only appear at the extreme rank (100), so tests must parametrize percentile_rank to include 0 and 100, not only a middle value. The nan-filtered test in sklearn/utils/tests/test_stats.py:test_weighted_percentile_nan_filtered compares against the same call on NaN-filtered input.
applies: sklearn/utils/stats.py _weighted_percentile, NaN handling and average=True interpolation
